title: secure-enclave: TouchID and FaceID on macOS
description:
No module exists. SPEC-HIRE specifies LocalAuthentication plus CryptoTokenKit, TouchID or FaceID acting as a platform FIDO2 authenticator, returning a Secure Enclave-backed assertion with a timestamp, at iaa3 with hardware presence.

WHY THIS RANKS ABOVE THE DAY-TWO SOURCES: with fido2, it is one of only two paths to real hardware presence, and it is the one that needs no separate device. On a Mac it is simply there. The persona-3tly presence model currently has no source that establishes presence at all, so both this and fido2 are what turn that model from theory into something testable.

PLATFORM CARE. persona-core is deliberately platform-independent and CI cross-checks it (the persona-core-must-stay-portable memory); this belongs in hire-attestors, not hire-core. The cfg(target_os = "macos") arms are NOT type-checked by a native Linux build -- that is the trap the portability job was added to catch, so 'make portability' must stay green while this lands.

Note tailscale.rs hardcodes /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock and therefore never activates on macOS, so this would be the first attestor that actually works there beyond unix-account.

Prompting attestor: same persona-jl4j.3 constraint as fido2.
acceptance_criteria: A Secure Enclave assertion over the daemon's challenge on real hardware; presence claimed only on actual user verification; make portability green.
